ledger.note: 24 February 1680: Saxe-Saalfeld. 'the Principality was divided on 24 February 1680 among his seven surviving sons. The lands of Saxe-Saalfeld went to the youngest of them, who became John Ernest IV (1658-1729)'; 'Saalfeld was the residence of the Dukes of Saxe-Saalfeld from 1680 to 1735'. (The lead: 'Established in 1699'; the text does not explain that date.)

6 August 1735: Coburg. After the dispute over Saxe-Coburg's 1699 inheritance 'was not settled until 1735', 'Most of the Saxe-Coburg properties were given to the new Ernestine line of Saxe-Saalfeld' (infobox 'Coburg and Saalfeld united: 6 August 1735'); Sonneberg and Neuhaus am Rennweg 'had to be handed over to Saxe-Meiningen' and Sonnefeld 'to Saxe-Hildburghausen'.
November 1806: the French. 'From November 1806 until the Peace of Tilsit in July 1807, the Principality was occupied by the French.' It entered the Confederation of the Rhine on 15 December 1806.
July 1807: the Peace of Tilsit ends the French occupation.

1815: Lichtenberg. At the Congress of Vienna it was sent 'an area left of the Rhine River, later called the Principality of Lichtenberg' ('a territorial gain as well as membership in the German Confederation for the sovereign'); the page names no giver.

region.text: the left-bank territory, later the Principality of Lichtenberg

ledger.note: 1826: Saalfeld. 'Most of Saxe-Hildburghausen and Saalfeld were given to Saxe-Meiningen along with a few various cities' (arbitration of 12 November 1826; the infobox: 'Lost Saalfeld, gained Gotha, renamed: 11 February 1826'). Saxe-Coburg gained the districts of Konigsberg and Sonnefeld from Saxe-Hildburghausen.

1826: Saxe-Coburg and Gotha. 'The new duchy of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha was born as a personal union of the two duchies of Saxe-Coburg and Saxe-Gotha.' 'Ernest III, the last Duke of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld, then became Ernest I, the first Duke of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha.'

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-3). New state: Cliopatria has no pre-1836 Saxe-Coburg row.

SCOPE. 1680 (Saxe-Saalfeld) to 1826, when the duchy lost Saalfeld and gained Gotha; the page's lead calls the line 'established in 1699'. A 1811 border treaty with Bavaria swapped four villages each way (Furth am Berg, Hof an der Steinach, Niederfullbach, Triebsdorf to Coburg; Gleussen, Buch am Forst, Herreth and a mill to Bavaria) and is not drawn. The page: the Principality 'underwent from 1773 onwards a forced management of debts by an Imperial Debit Commission until 1802'. Wars: Frederick Josias fought in the Austro-Turkish War and the War of the First Coalition (no years), and the Principality fought on the Allied side in 1813; no war entries.

SHAPES. Saalfeld 11.37E 50.65N 12 km; Coburg 10.96E 50.26N 10 km; Lichtenberg 7.12E 49.47N 15 km. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Saalfeld', 'Coburg', 'St. Wendel' (Lichtenberg).

NOT SETTLED. (1) The page's 1699 date; (2) the 1735 shares (Sonneberg, Neuhaus am Rennweg to Meiningen; Sonnefeld to Hildburghausen; one-third of Romhild and five-twelfths of Themar stayed with Coburg); (3) 11 February against 12 November 1826; (4) Cliopatria's Saxe-Coburg and Gotha row starts in 1836 and leaves 1826-36 empty.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: Saxe-Meiningen before 1820 and Saxe-Hildburghausen.
